title: How to learn good representations by prediction?
reading: The slide asks how masked-prediction pretraining can yield good representations, and answers by contrasting two masking ratios applied to the same cheetah photograph. A side-by-side comparison of light versus heavy masking carries the argument; captions label the left as a small masked portion and the right as a large masked portion.

visuals.description: Two versions of a cheetah photo. Left: a single small grey square patch occluding part of the animal's shoulder, captioned 'Small portion: May not require a high-level understanding'. Right: the same image with most patches replaced by grey, only scattered fragments visible, captioned 'Large portion: Encourage to learn semantic features'.
visuals.assertion: Masking only a small region lets the model reconstruct from local low-level cues, whereas masking a large portion forces it to learn semantic, high-level features.

concepts.name: Masked image prediction / masking ratio
concepts.why_it_matters: The fraction of the image hidden determines whether the pretext task is trivially local or demands semantic understanding.

concepts.name: Semantic features vs low-level cues
concepts.why_it_matters: Motivates high masking ratios in self-supervised methods like MAE.
